answer: An attacker who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the falcon history. Churn is counted in tide, and lagoon publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 8% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 82 account operation therefore ties up 8 million dollars of idle capital. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
